🇲🇽🏭 NEARSHORING HOLDS: $4.1 BILLION LANDS IN GUANAJUATO

Even PAN-run Guanajuato makes the nearshoring case: $4.132 billion in foreign investment across 61 projects since September 2024, over 15,000 jobs, and the state now expects to reach 70% of its six-year $8-billion goal by year's end (El Economista). This year alone: $718 million and 4,386 new jobs in auto parts, agro-industry and metalworking — tariffs and all.

🇲🇽✊ MEXICO CITY BRINGS 197,000 DOMESTIC WORKERS OUT OF THE SHADOWS

Mexico City is formalizing a workforce long left informal: 197,000 domestic workers — 91.9% of them women — with only 12,000 currently in the social-security system. The city's labor office gave 2,500 women free legal counsel, ran a mobile "Afiliatón" to enroll them in IMSS, and published an ILO-backed "Guide to Domestic Work with Rights." "Household and care work sustains life," the Women's Ministry noted, "but for decades has disproportionately fallen on women."

🇲🇽🛡️ STATE OF MEXICO HOMICIDES DOWN 58% IN UNDER TWO YEARS

Intentional homicides in the State of Mexico fell 58% from September 2024 to June 2026 — 6.6 daily victims down to 2.8, the lowest average since 2017, per the SESNSP. Vehicle theft dropped 59%, armed robbery of businesses 56%. Security Minister Omar García Harfuch credited the Unified Command "sharing intelligence, planning joint operations and responding more rapidly" across 15 priority municipalities.

🚨🇲🇽 THE PLAYBOOK TO DESTABILIZE MEXICO HAS A GUEST LIST

Contralínea maps the machinery: Larry Rubin — a dual US-Mexican citizen heading the "American Society of Mexico" — hosted a June 6 dinner uniting opposition figures and friendly media, all amplifying the "narco-government" line that invites US intervention. Rubin openly floats a bilateral "crime-fighting treaty" that would put US agents on Mexican soil. Sheinbaum called it out from the podium days later.

🌽🇲🇽 MEXICO IMPORTS MORE CORN THAN EVER — 95% OF IT US YELLOW CORN

Mexico imported a record 12.28 million tons of corn in Jan–June 2026 — up 8.6% year-on-year, worth $2.539 billion, per customs agency ANAM. Almost all of it, 11.7M tons of yellow corn, comes from the US for animal feed — while white-corn imports fell 15.9%, the grain Mexico still grows for its own tortillas. Food sovereignty is the fight the 4T's grain self-sufficiency plan is built for.

🇲🇽🌎 WASHINGTON TIES T-MEC RENEWAL TO MEXICO'S WATER

US Trade Rep Jamieson Greer says it will be "difficult" for Trump to renew the T-MEC unless Mexico cooperates on border security and delivers water owed under the 1944 treaty — said openly, mid-negotiation, as the third round of talks wraps in Mexico City. A continental trade review, turned into leverage over a shared river in a drought year.

🐉🇲🇽 China's Carmakers Built a $100 Billion Global Footprint — and Mexico Is on the Map

Chinese automakers have poured over $100 billion into overseas EV and battery plants since 2019, outspending US rivals by 4-to-6x on international projects, per Rhodium Group data reported this month. The strategy is blunt: build factories in Hungary, Indonesia, Morocco — and Mexico — that create local jobs and local political constituencies too valuable to shut down.

“Companies like BYD are becoming essentially the new GMs and Fords of the EV era,” one analyst put it. Mexico sits at the center of that shift — courted as a manufacturing base for the whole hemisphere even as Washington uses the USMCA review to pressure it into slamming the door on Chinese capital.

Mexico's play isn't to pick a side — it's to keep the door open on its own terms. Foreign capital, jobs and technology are leverage, not a threat. In a world where the real risk is depending on one partner who governs by tariff, more options is more sovereignty.

🌐🇲🇽 Latin America Writes Its Own Playbook — Without Washington's Permission

The First Russia–Latin America Strategic Cooperation Forum (CORAL 2026) wrapped in São Paulo on July 16, drawing delegations from Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, Venezuela, Ecuador, Paraguay and beyond. Organizers called it the most significant act of public diplomacy between the two regions in 20 years.

Delegates launched a 200-page strategic compendium and a Programme of Action spanning trade, science and technology — a concrete architecture for cooperation that routes around the G7. Latin America, one coordinator noted, is “a pluralistic region rich in natural resources critically important for modern economic production.”

For Mexico the lesson is the one Sheinbaum's government keeps repeating: sovereignty means multiplying partners, not swapping one master for another. A multipolar world is one where the Global South sets its own terms — and no single capital gets a veto.
📸 Mañanera del Pueblo — Toluca, Estado de México, 22 de julio de 2026
